metadata.title: Brutalist Progress — Week 1
metadata.greeting_note: English greeting, not a world-language hello — matches the required submission intro line spoken aloud in B00 ('Hi, I am Kavya...'). Presenter is Kavya Mehta, not the claude-liam/Nik Bear Brown persona: no IN-FOR-BEAR framing, no @NikBearBrown branding anywhere in this reel. ClaudeTitleOutro was deliberately NOT used for the outro because its '@NikBearBrown' handle is hardcoded in the component source (runtime/remotion/src/scenes/ClaudeTitleOutro.tsx:19) with no prop override — using it here would misattribute this personal project. ClaudeVerdictArtifact (no hardcoded branding) is used as the closing card instead, same pattern as kavya-cabstream-week1-progress.
metadata.note: ai-explainer recap of this session's own real, verifiable work setting up and debugging the Brutalist toolkit on Kavya's machine — not an illustrative/constructed example. Every bug cited is real and traced to an actual file/line fixed this session: pronunciation.py:23 (UnicodeDecodeError, cp1252 default encoding), remotion_scenes.py (bare 'npx' string -> WinError2, fixed via shutil.which), runtime/remotion node_modules (never installed, ran npm install), compile.py's drawtext fontfile= (Windows drive-letter colon broke the ffmpeg filtergraph parser, fixed via relpath), runtime/qc/final_frame_check.py (BURN_IN_EXCLUDE only covered the bottom-left per-beat label, not the top-right review timecode, causing every beat to false-positive as edge-bleed), and a ReqBars authoring error (multiplier values fed into a 0-100%-scale component, overflowing the bar). No code beats -- output-only cards. Built to satisfy docs/FELLOWS-SUBMISSION.md's required-content rules: the required intro line ('Hi, I am [name] and this video is about...') opens B00's narration verbatim, AI-narration is disclosed in the same beat, and this reel renders native 16:9 (3840x2160) and 9:16 (2160x3840) rather than a crop of one master. Brutalist version/commit for this build should be recorded in the submission README against the repo's current HEAD at build time.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about my first week setting up and debugging the Brutalist video pipeline. This narration is AI-generated with Kokoro text-to-speech, reading a script I wrote and reviewed. Week one wasn't a clean build — it was six small breaks, each one traced and fixed. Here's what actually happened, and what's true about the pipeline now.

beats.narration_text: Strip the pipeline down and it's four stages. A beat sheet, authored by hand. Kokoro audio, which measures real durations before anything else renders. Remotion render and ffmpeg compile. And QC gates that check type, layout, and facts before anything ships. Every one of these four broke at least once this week.

beats.narration_text: Four things actually happened. The toolkit itself needed setup — nothing was pre-installed. The first reel got authored end to end. Six real pipeline bugs surfaced and got fixed, not patched around. And two finished videos shipped, sixteen-by-nine and nine-by-sixteen, both clean.

beats.narration_text: Three of the six, to start. A Windows file-encoding crash reading a pronunciation table. A silent failure because Windows needs npx-dot-c-m-d, not bare npx. And Node dependencies that were simply never installed — the setup script had skipped that step.

shot.visual_intent: Output-only terminal card, no source shown. Three numbered findings print in sync with narration.

show.event: terminal window, 'WEEK 1 — BUGS FOUND' header types
'1. UnicodeDecodeError' prints
'2. WinError 2: npx is npx.cmd on Windows' prints, terracotta wash
'3. node_modules/: never installed' prints; all three hold

out.text: 2. WinError 2: npx is npx.cmd on Windows, not npx

beats.narration_text: The other three. An ffmpeg filter choking on a Windows drive-letter colon in a font path. A visual QC checker flagging every single beat as broken — it never excluded the review timestamp from its own corner check. And a chart fed the wrong kind of number, overflowing its own frame. Each one traced to its actual line, then fixed.

beats.narration_text: Recap: the toolkit needed real setup, nothing was pre-installed. Six bugs surfaced across audio, render, compile, and QC — each one fixed at the root, not patched over. One reel shipped end to end, two formats, zero blocking defects. The honest read: a working pipeline isn't one that never breaks. It's one where every break actually gets found.
